title: Project Setup & Architecture
description: Plan the full‑stack blog, install dependencies, set up Prisma with models, and configure NextAuth.

slides.title: The Capstone: A Complete Blog Platform 🎯
slides.content:
# What We'll Build

A public‑facing blog with:

* **Posts** list with pagination.
* **Individual post** page with full content.
* **Comments** section under each post (authenticated users only).
* **Admin dashboard** (previous chapter) for managing posts.
* **Authentication** via GitHub (NextAuth).
* **Database** with Prisma and SQLite (or PostgreSQL).
* **Styling** with Tailwind CSS.
* **SEO** with Metadata API.
* **Deployment** to Vercel.

This pulls together every concept from the course.

slides.title: Step 1: Create the Project & Dependencies 📦
slides.content:
# Setup Commands

```bash
npx create-next-app@latest my-blog --tailwind --eslint
cd my-blog
npm install next-auth prisma @prisma/client zod
npm install --save-dev prisma
npx prisma init --datasource-provider sqlite
```

We'll add more packages later. The `--tailwind` flag sets up Tailwind CSS automatically.

slides.title: Step 2: Database Schema 🗃️
slides.content:
# Prisma Models

We need three models:
* `User` – managed by NextAuth (or we can let NextAuth create it).
* `Post` – blog posts with slug, title, content, published, and author.
* `Comment` – linked to a post and a user.

We'll also add a `Category` model if we want. For simplicity, we'll start with Post and Comment.

slides.title: prisma/schema.prisma
slides.content: Define the models and run `npx prisma migrate dev --name init`.
slides.codeSnippet:
model User {
  id        String    @id @default(cuid())
  name      String?
  email     String?   @unique
  image     String?
  posts     Post[]
  comments  Comment[]
}

model Post {
  id        String    @id @default(cuid())
  slug      String    @unique
  title     String
  content   String
  published Boolean   @default(false)
  createdAt DateTime  @default(now())
  author    User      @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
  authorId  String
  comments  Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  text      String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  post      Post     @relation(fields: [postId], references: [id])
  postId    String
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  userId    String
}

quizData.question: Why is the `slug` field marked as `@unique`?

options.text: To make it the primary key
To ensure no two posts have the same URL‑friendly identifier
Because Prisma requires all text fields to be unique

quizData.explanation: The slug is used in the URL (`/posts/my-post`). Uniqueness prevents routing conflicts.

slides.title: Step 3: Configure NextAuth 🛡️
slides.content:
# Authentication Setup

We'll use the GitHub provider as in Chapter 7.

1. Create `lib/auth.js` with `authOptions`.
2. Add `pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].js` (App Router uses `app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.js`).
3. Set environment variables in `.env.local`.

We'll need NextAuth to attach the Prisma adapter later, but initially, JWT sessions are enough.

slides.title: NextAuth API Route (app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.js)
slides.content: App Router version using the route handler.

quizData.question: In the App Router, how do you export the NextAuth handler?

options.text: Export named GET and POST functions pointing to the same handler
There's no support for NextAuth in App Router

quizData.explanation: App Router API routes use the `route.js` file with exported functions for each HTTP method.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content: For local development, generate the `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` with `openssl rand -base64 32`. Store it in `.env.local`. Never commit secret keys.
